citeAs: Badertdinov, I., Golubev, A., Nekrashevich, M., Shevtsov, A., Karasik, S., Andriushchenko, A., Trofimova, M., Litvintseva, D., Yangel, B. (2025). SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel (Nebius)
description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset of over 21,000 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks extracted from real-world GitHub repositories via a fully automated pipeline. Each task instance is grounded in a real GitHub issue and its corresponding pull request, providing executable environments suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale. The dataset includes quality annotations (issue clarity, task complexity, test patch correctness) generated by a fine-tuned LLM.
name: SWE-rebench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model was evaluated on a 413-example validation set. For Task Complexity: 81% accuracy, weighted F1 of 0.82 (vs. baseline 68% accuracy). For Test Patch Correctness: 67% accuracy, weighted F1 of 0.65. For Issue Clarity: 79% accuracy, weighted F1 of 0.76. Detailed precision and recall per class are reported in Table 4 of the paper.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Automated annotation using a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model; no external crowdsourcing platform was used. Distributed computing via TractoAI platform was used for pipeline execution.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated quality assessment was performed by fine-tuning Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict three binary quality labels per task: (1) Issue Clarity — whether the GitHub issue description is sufficiently detailed; (2) Task Complexity — estimated effort to resolve the issue; (3) Test Patch Correctness — whether tests accurately verify the intended fix. Each task instance is assessed for each quality characteristic separately using a 75/25 training/validation split (total 413 validation examples). Labels are provided as metadata with each task instance.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to Python repositories with permissive licenses where Python constitutes over 75% of codebase lines, which may bias the distribution toward certain types of projects. The benchmark subset requires issues created in 2025 and problem statements in English, which may introduce recency and language biases. The automated quality assessment model was trained on SWE-bench Verified annotations, which may propagate any biases present in that dataset.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected via an automated four-stage pipeline: (1) Preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub repositories — approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025, from over 30,000 repositories with permissive licenses where Python constitutes over 75% of codebase lines; (2) Automated installation instruction configuration using an LLM (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct) to generate environment setup recipes; (3) Execution-based installation verification in isolated containers; (4) Automated instance quality assessment using a fine-tuned LLM. The pipeline yielded 21,336 valid task instances from 3,468 distinct GitHub repositories.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of GitHub pull requests and issues sourced from GitHub Archive (a daily JSON archive of all public GitHub events) and directly cloned GitHub repositories with full commit histories. Approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues from over 30,000 repositories were downloaded as the initial raw input.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues and pull requests created before May 1, 2025 were collected. The benchmark subset uses tasks from 2025 (January and March–April 2025 subsets are specifically analyzed).
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: 1. Automated task quality assessment may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. 2. The initial release is limited exclusively to Python, restricting applicability to other language ecosystems. 3. The automated pipeline relies on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations that may not capture every project's subtleties. 4. The LLM-based approach for generating installation instructions was validated on only 18 repositories for prompt engineering.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Task instances were grouped by project version (normalized to major.minor format). For each version group, the base_commit of the most recent pull request was selected. Patches were generated by diffing head_commit against base_commit (falling back to merge_commit if head_commit unavailable). Test directives were filtered to exclude deleted files. Tasks with flaky tests (external API calls or floating-point precision issues) were excluded by running tests multiple times. Dependency versions were pinned after successful setup.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering criteria applied to raw pull requests: (1) issue from a Python repository with a permissive license; (2) issue marked as resolved; (3) PR merged into main branch; (4) PR not linked to multiple issues; (5) issue description longer than 10 characters; (6) PR introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files; (7) changes affect 1 to 15 files. Each PR's overall patch was split into a solution patch (non-test file changes) and a test patch (test file changes only). Repository versions were normalized to major.minor format. Dependency versions were frozen via pip freeze and conda env export after successful setup.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The pipeline is designed for continuous collection of fresh tasks. A public leaderboard (https://swe-rebench.com/leaderboard) is continuously updated with new evaluations. Future work includes expanding data coverage, improving task filtering, supporting new programming languages, and keeping the benchmark up-to-date with fresh tasks for existing and new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: SWE-rebench may accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns and contributes to responsible advancement of the field.
rai:dataUseCases: 1. Training LLM-based software engineering agents, particularly via reinforcement learning. 2. Evaluating LLM-based agents on real-world software engineering tasks in a contamination-free setting. 3. Benchmarking agent performance with standardized, reproducible evaluation protocols. 4. Studying data contamination effects in existing benchmarks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (used for generating installation recipes and for automated quality assessment after fine-tuning on SWE-bench Verified annotations). The agentless approach inspired by Agentless [Xia et al., 2024] was used for environment setup instruction generation.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper describes three quality labels per item but does not specify a number of independent human annotations per item; annotation is automated via fine-tuned LLM.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotation is performed by an automated fine-tuned LLM model, not human annotators; no human annotator demographics are described.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling beyond filtering out invalid tasks; no specific missing data protocol is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; invalid tasks are excluded rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of GitHub issues, pull requests, and code from public repositories; no personal or sensitive information collection is described.
